What gets in the way today

{{icon:circle-alert}}

Complex collateral and asset coverage

Establishing real asset backing and depreciation-adjusted net block values is hard when several lenders hold charges over equipment and inventory.

{{icon:circle-alert}}

Unreported related-party leaks

Borrowers can quietly channel high-yield private credit into sister concerns or subsidiaries through unsecured inter-corporate loans.

{{icon:circle-alert}}

Subordinated debt structuring

Structuring mezzanine or structured facilities depends on knowing exact creditor seniority and historical charge creation dates.

{{icon:circle-alert}}

Inflated working capital

Inflated trade receivables or stagnant inventory can sit deep inside unlisted borrowers’ balance sheet schedules.

{{icon:circle-alert}}

High-risk monitoring overhead

High-yield lending needs continuous tracking of borrower filing delays, address changes and capital changes.

{{icon:circle-alert}}

Personal guarantee vetting

Guarantors’ net worth, active directorships and existing corporate liabilities are hard to cross-check before a loan is sanctioned.
